title: U.S. House · California's 28th District
area: The San Gabriel Valley in Los Angeles County, including Monterey Park, Alhambra, El Monte, and the Linda Vista area of Pasadena. District lines were redrawn for the 2026 election under California Proposition 50.

context.text: California redrew its congressional district lines for the 2026 election cycle after voters approved Proposition 50 on November 4, 2025, a mid-decade redistricting measure.
Incumbent Democrat Judy Chu, first elected in 2009, and Republican April Verlato, a former mayor of Arcadia, advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary.

summary.text: Judy Chu is the Democratic incumbent for California's 28th Congressional District, first elected in a July 2009 special election. A psychologist who taught in the Los Angeles community college system, she held local and state offices in the San Gabriel Valley, including three terms as mayor of Monterey Park, before entering Congress as the first Chinese American woman elected to the House. She serves on the Ways and Means and Budget committees.

background.text: Born in Los Angeles, California, on July 7, 1953.
Earned a bachelor's degree from UCLA in 1974 and a Ph.D. from the California School of Professional Psychology in 1979.
Worked as a professor at Los Angeles City College and East Los Angeles College.
Was first elected to the Garvey School District Board of Education in 1985, then to the Monterey Park City Council in 1988, where she served as mayor three times.
Served in the California State Assembly (49th District) from 2001 to 2006, and was then elected to the State Board of Equalization, California's elected tax board.
Won a July 2009 special election to the U.S. House and became the first Chinese American woman elected to Congress.

Serves on the House Ways and Means Committee, where she is a member of its Health, Worker and Family Support, and Oversight subcommittees, and on the House Budget Committee; she is also a member of the House Democratic Caucus Steering and Policy Committee.
Was elected chair of the Congressional Asian Pacific American Caucus in 2011 and served in that role until 2025; she founded and co-chairs the Congressional Creative Rights Caucus.

Her official biography lists among her accomplishments a congressional resolution of regret for the Chinese Exclusion Act of 1882, the designation of the San Gabriel Mountains as a national monument, and a requirement that the Department of Defense address military hazing.
According to her official biography, she lives in Monterey Park with her husband, Michael Eng, and they have been residents there for over 30 years.

priorities.text: Protecting and expanding the Affordable Care Act and the Medicare program, and lowering prescription drug costs.
Taking aggressive action to halt and reverse the effects of climate change and end reliance on fossil fuels.
Reforming the immigration system, including a pathway to citizenship for DACA, TPS, and DED recipients and modernizing family-based immigration.

positions.summary: Says she is committed to protecting and expanding the Affordable Care Act and Medicare, and is a founding member of the Medicare for All Caucus.
positions.quote: I am committed to working to protect and expand the Affordable Care Act (ACA), as well as protecting the Medicare program so we can ensure our seniors have quality care they can count on.

positions.summary: Says she supports aggressive action to combat the climate crisis and reach a net-zero economy, and voted for the Inflation Reduction Act's clean-energy tax credits.
positions.quote: I support aggressive action to combat the climate crisis and meet President Biden’s goal of a net-zero economy by midcentury.

positions.summary: Describes the administration's deportation agenda as putting rights at risk and has cosponsored legislation to give DACA, TPS, and DED recipients a path to citizenship rather than expanding enforcement.
positions.quote: the Trump administration’s anti-immigrant, mass deportation agenda has put all of our rights at risk

positions.summary: Criticized the administration's broad tariffs as a tax increase that raises prices for consumers, while saying targeted tariffs can have a legitimate role in addressing unfair trade practices.
positions.quote: Today, he is extending the same treatment to millions of products, immediately imposing the largest tax increase in history and raising costs for every single American.

positions.summary: Says healthcare choices, including reproductive decisions, should be made by women rather than employers or politicians, and is a member of the Congressional Pro-Choice Caucus.
positions.quote: healthcare choices should be made by women, not their employers or politicians

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Ways and Means (Health Subcommittee; Oversight Subcommittee; Work and Welfare Subcommittee) and the House Committee on the Budget in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).
Introduced H.R. 2928, the Mortgage Relief for Disaster Survivors Act, to provide mortgage forbearance for homeowners in presidentially declared disaster areas.

candidates.name: April Verlato
candidates.currentRole: Former Mayor of Arcadia, California (mayor beginning 2020; Arcadia City Council member since 2016)

summary.text: April Verlato is the Republican nominee for California's 28th Congressional District. An attorney and businesswoman born and raised in Arcadia, she was elected to the Arcadia City Council in 2016 and has served as the city's mayor. She ran against Rep. Judy Chu in 2024 and is running again in 2026.

background.text: Born and raised in Arcadia, California.
Earned a bachelor's degree in political science from UCLA and a law degree from Southwestern School of Law.
Has worked as a businesswoman and an attorney.
Was elected to the Arcadia City Council in 2016 and later served as mayor of Arcadia.

Her campaign website, as excerpted by Ballotpedia, says she led the revitalization of Downtown Arcadia and was a founding board member of the Downtown Arcadia Improvement Association, a Community Benefits District, and that she supported creation of the San Gabriel Valley Regional Housing Trust Fund.
Was the Republican candidate against Judy Chu in the November 2024 general election for this seat; Chu won.

priorities.text: Campaign platform emphasizes fiscal responsibility, support for law enforcement, national security, border security, market-driven healthcare solutions, veterans' needs, and reducing the national debt.
Cites leading the revitalization of Downtown Arcadia as mayor, including work to attract small businesses and events to the area.

researchNotes: Judy Chu has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey; positions and priorities were drawn from her official House issues pages and press releases. Her federal floor votes and FEC totals are added separately by script. April Verlato has not completed the 2026 survey either; her campaign-website statements (quoted by Ballotpedia) were general enough that specific issue-key positions were not confidently attributable, so positions are omitted per the research standard. Biography expansion: Judy Chu's biography draws on her official House biography page, Ballotpedia and Wikipedia (her birth year is from Wikipedia only; bioguide.congress.gov could not be used); April Verlato has no official bio page found and her mayoral dates differ between sources, so they are omitted.
